# Guarded daily maintenance

The scheduled workflow first repairs default-branch npm lock synchronization and
formatting of existing workflow YAML without an AI request. It opens one draft PR
for review, then defers dependency/improvement work until that PR is resolved.

Workflow changes are accepted only when parsing before and after produces the
same typed YAML data. New/deleted workflow files, duplicate YAML keys, symlinks,
permission changes, modified commands and semantic edits are rejected. Lockfiles
are generated by npm, never supplied to the AI agent for editing. Only a recognized
`npm ci` lock synchronization failure permits regeneration; network, authentication
and dependency-resolution failures remain failures.

The AI dependency-repair path considers up to three failing same-repository bot
PRs. Its source-file allowlist excludes workflows, lockfiles, credentials and
policy files. Both supported GitHub CLI bot identities (`app/renovate`,
`app/dependabot`) and canonical `[bot]` identities are recognized exactly; bare
usernames are rejected. RepoMap is disabled so aider creates no checkout cache;
explicitly supplied source targets still provide context. Protected bytes, tracked file sets, Git HEAD and index are verified.
Lint, tests and build must pass before any commit is published. Provider failures
(including an exhausted balance with a zero aider exit status) fail the job.

These are change-publication guards, not a sandbox for executing repository code.
No credentials, token scopes, branch protections or billing settings are added.
Checkout credentials are not persisted, package validation receives no GitHub or
OpenAI token environment variables, and publishing uses a command-local credential
helper. These precautions do not turn project-code execution into a sandbox.
Existing green dependency-PR merge rules are retained.

## Verification and limitations

Run `python -m unittest discover -s .github/maintenance -p 'test_*.py'` and
`bash -n .github/maintenance/maintenance.sh`. Python requires `PyYAML==6.0.3`.
The guard-test job runs on maintenance pull requests without write permissions.

A draft PR is not evidence of passing remote CI. GitHub may require a maintainer
to approve workflow runs created by `GITHUB_TOKEN` events. Existing token or
organization restrictions can also reject workflow-file pushes or PR creation;
the run reports those failures rather than adding access. If pushing a default-
branch repair fails, its patch is retained as a workflow artifact when available.
Maintainers must review the exact commit and its checks before merging.
